solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Guide for driver reversing vehicle at end of test

indicators.note: at end of places the turned vehicle after the test word

parts.note: SAT is a standard abbreviation for a Standard Assessment Test or Scholastic Aptitude Test

indicators.note: reversing tells us the vehicle word is written backwards

explanation.surface: A learner driver backs a vehicle up at the close of a driving test, needing guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite navigation device gives a motorist directions, so it guides whoever is behind the wheel.

clue.text: On board ship, I hurried over for cocktails

indicators.note: on board means placed inside the letters for a steamship, as if carried aboard

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

indicators.note: over in a down clue signals the hurried word read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: Someone rushes across a ship's deck to fetch the cocktails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' gives DECAR; 'On board' uses the convention that anything aboard a ship sits between the S and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice, so the plural names several such drinks.

clue.text: Might I stir up trouble after a drink? Yes

definitions.text: Might I stir up trouble after a drink? Yes

indicators.note: after puts the reversed trouble word behind the drink in this down entry
stir up in a down clue signals the trouble word being turned upwards, read backwards

explanation.surface: A rowdy youngster asks whether a drink will set them off causing mayhem, and answers yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir up' turns WAR into RAW. The whole clue is the young hooligan's own question and answer, so it also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearaway is an unruly, reckless young person, exactly someone likely to cause mayhem once lubricated.

clue.text: Regularly carried near stadium

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words carried near, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Something was carried to a place close to the stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed space for sport or spectacle, so it is a near synonym for a sports ground.

clue.text: Put forward on behalf of poet

parts.note: pro means for, on behalf of
Ezra Pound was an American poet

explanation.surface: Someone presents an idea on behalf of a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: To propound a theory is to offer it up for consideration, i.e. to advance or propose it.

clue.text: Feel dizzy, holding rope attached to dog having name on disc

indicators.note: holding means the dizzy word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: to reel is to feel giddy and stagger

indicators.note: attached to joins the dog straight after the rope

parts.note: a cord is a thin rope
lab is short for Labrador, a dog breed

explanation.surface: A giddy dog walker clutches a lead attached to a dog wearing a name tag disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'name on disc' looks like a dog's tag but means the company name printed on a record.
explanation.definitionFit: A record label is the company whose name is printed on the centre of a vinyl record, so the name on a disc.

clue.text: Customer turned up before 'Archers' broadcast

indicators.note: before places the turned word ahead of the rearranged letters
turned means the word up is written backwards
broadcast means scattered, so the letters of Archers are rearranged

explanation.surface: A listener arrives early for a broadcast of the radio soap The Archers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap about country life. 'turned' gives PU and 'broadcast' gives RCHASER.
explanation.definitionFit: A purchaser is a buyer, which is what a customer is in a shop.

clue.text: Not vain, presumably, in posh fur

explanation.surface: Someone modest despite being dressed in expensive fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vain' looks like conceited, but the definition plays on 'in vain', meaning to no use.
explanation.definitionFit: Something serviceable is not used in vain, hence the punning 'presumably' and the question-like hedge.

clue.text: Put off entertaining one person unlikely to eat much

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A host cancels a dinner party because one guest barely eats.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on a slimming regime restricts their food, so they are unlikely to eat a lot.

clue.text: Trader supplying venison, not quite all for consumption

indicators.note: for consumption means taken in, as food is, so the shortened word goes inside

parts.note: venison is the meat of deer

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter of all is dropped

explanation.surface: A trader sells venison but keeps some back for eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' leaves AL; 'for consumption' means eaten, so taken inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer is someone who buys and sells goods, so a merchant or trader.

clue.text: So-called gangster rarely spotted without female on arm, for a start

indicators.note: without means outside, so the scarce word goes around the other letters
for a start means the first letter of arm

explanation.surface: A notorious gangster is seldom seen without a woman on his arm.
explanation.walkthrough: F and A go inside SCARCE. 'without' here means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was nicknamed Scarface after facial wounds, so it is a gangster's so-called name.

clue.text: Letter card

definitions.meaning: a single written symbol such as A or B
an eccentric, amusing person, as in 'what a card'

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a written symbol in an alphabet and an odd, entertaining individual.

clue.text: Youngster tapes American hit on particular 5

indicators.note: tapes means binds round, so the youngster word wraps the next pieces

parts.note: a tot is a small child
to lam is to beat or hit

explanation.surface: A child records an American chart hit on a particular record label.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition '5' points to the answer at 5 down, so this is a kind of record company; 'tapes' means binds round.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the famous Detroit soul company's UK imprint, so it is an example of a record company.

clue.text: Challenging piece for orchestra

indicators.note: piece means a portion of the word Challenging supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A difficult work for an orchestra to play.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hallé is a famous Manchester orchestra; 'piece' looks like a musical work but signals a part of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hallé is a symphony orchestra based in Manchester, founded by Charles Hallé.

clue.text: Reconvenes rebel masses after revolution

indicators.note: after revolution means the letters of rebel masses have been turned upside down and rearranged

explanation.surface: After an uprising, the rebellious crowd gathers once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconvene is to gather again after a break, the same as coming together once more.

clue.text: PA getting confidential note from Mr Barlow

indicators.note: from means the note is taken away from the name

parts.note: Gary Barlow is the Take That singer

explanation.surface: A personal assistant receives a private memo from a Mr Barlow.
explanation.walkthrough: Gary Barlow is the lead singer of British boy band Take That. 'note from' removes G from GARY, leaving ARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A PA is a personal assistant, who handles office work and correspondence for an employer.

clue.text: Stopped at home after announcement of treaty

indicators.note: after places the home word behind the spoken word
announcement of means the treaty word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

explanation.surface: Talks stalled at home once a treaty was announced.
explanation.definitionFit: To have packed in something is to have quit or given it up, an informal synonym for ceased.

clue.text: In French a barbed comment is demeaning

parts.note: a dig is a pointed remark

explanation.surface: A sneering jibe delivered in French is belittling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag means beneath one's dignity, so something degrading or unbecoming.

clue.text: A Liberal returned to House of Commons, elected PM

parts.note: the Commons is a parliamentary chamber

indicators.note: returned means the letters for a liberal are written backwards

parts.note: in means elected, as a party voted into office

explanation.surface: A Liberal goes back to Parliament and is chosen as Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns AL into LA, which goes after CHAMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Neville Chamberlain was British Prime Minister from 1937 to 1940, so a former premier.

clue.text: In class, is teacher providing help?

indicators.note: in means the letters lie within the words class, is teacher

explanation.surface: A pupil wonders whether the classroom teacher is offering support.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to give aid, the same as helping.

clue.text: Frightful scare about a ruler

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the a
frightful means horribly mangled, so the letters of scare are rearranged

explanation.surface: A terrible fright concerning a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frightful' rearranges SCARE to CAESR, which goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar was the title of Roman emperors, so a ruler or autocrat.

clue.text: Fish consumed after request to skip starter

indicators.note: after places the consumed word behind the shortened request
skip starter means the first letter of the request word is left out

explanation.surface: A diner eats fish after asking to miss the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skip starter' looks like a menu instruction; it cuts ASK to SK.
explanation.definitionFit: The skate is a flat cartilaginous sea fish eaten widely in Britain.

clue.text: Surprisingly not like a river boat

indicators.note: surprisingly means arranged in an unexpected way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Oddly, this vessel is nothing like a river craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanker carrying oil is a large ship, a vessel used at sea.

clue.text: Getting on, and coping without man

indicators.note: without means the man word is taken out

explanation.surface: An elderly person is growing older and managing fine on their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for growing old, as in 'he's getting on a bit'.

clue.text: Fashionable blue retro little numbers now available

parts.note: the blue is a poetic term for the sea

indicators.note: retro means backwards, so the letters for little numbers are reversed

parts.note: nos is the short form of numbers

explanation.surface: Trendy retro blue items in small sizes are now on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retro' reads like fashion jargon but turns NOS into SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is in season is currently on sale, being at its natural time of harvest.

clue.text: Objected to daughter wearing denim pants

indicators.note: wearing means the daughter is inside, dressed in the shuffled letters
pants is slang for rubbish, so the letters of denim are messed up

explanation.surface: Someone disliked their daughter wearing denim trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' in British slang means poor, rubbish; it rearranges DENIM to MINED, which takes D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: If you minded something you disliked it, a mild synonym for protested against.

clue.text: A lawyer ultimately interrupts hearing, using delaying tactics?

indicators.note: interrupts means breaks into the hearing word

parts.note: trying a case is hearing it in court

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of lawyer

explanation.surface: A barrister keeps breaking into a court hearing to stall it.
explanation.walkthrough: A and R go inside TRYING.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to linger or dawdle, so lingering is putting things off, hence the question mark.

clue.text: About noon, like having giant drink

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the giant word goes round noon's letter

parts.note: Gog is a legendary giant, as in Gog and Magog

explanation.surface: Around midday, a giant has a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a festive beverage of eggs, milk, sugar and often spirits.
